name: Randomized Littlestone Dimension
definition: The **Randomized Littlestone Dimension** of $\mathcal H$ is $\mathrm{RL}(\mathcal H)=\frac12\sup_T \mathbb E_T$, where $T$ ranges over binary decision trees shattered by $\mathcal H$ and $\mathbb E_T$ is the root-to-leaf length when, at every internal node, the next edge is chosen uniformly at random.
graph_summary: Half the largest average branch length of a binary tree shattered by the class.
origin_references: Introduced by Filmus, Hanneke, Mehalel, and Moran \cite{filmus2023randomized}.

monotonic.proof: Every tree shattered by a subfamily is also shattered by the containing class.

p_monotonic.proof: A tree shattered by a coordinate projection queries only retained coordinates; lifting its realizing projected hypotheses gives a tree shattered by the original class.

doubly_monotonic.proof: The preceding subfamily and projection arguments establish both required forms of monotonicity.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection.

strict_c_monotonic.proof: For a one-coordinate split, the whole class contains each conditioned branch as a subfamily. If their values differ it therefore exceeds the smaller one; if they agree, joining near-optimal trees below a root querying that coordinate raises the average-depth value by one half.

strictly_monotonic.proof: The parameter is doubly monotonic, vanishes only on classes with at most one hypothesis, and is strictly c-monotonic by the tree-grafting argument.

tight_strict_c_monotonic.proof: For the two constant hypotheses, either active coordinate has two singleton conditioned branches, both of randomized Littlestone value 0, whereas the whole class has value 1/2 rather than 1. Thus the equal-branch +1 requirement fails.
